title: Conversations in Space: Non-Linear LLM Interaction in Everyday Use
abstract: arXiv:2605.15848v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: As LLM conversations grow, their histories capture alternative directions, decisions, and evolving lines of thought that can be difficult to navigate through chat alone. We investigate an interaction concept that represents the same conversation through two synchronized views: a familiar linear chat for ongoing dialogue and a spatial canvas for navigating its emerging structure. To investigate this interaction concept, we developed CanvasConvo, which allows conversations to branch into alternative paths that remain accessible across both views. In a five-day field deployment with 24 participants, we examined how people appropriated this parallel representation in self-directed knowledge work. Participants selectively moved between the two views rather than replacing chat with the canvas. Chat remained central to conversational interaction, while the canvas supported overview, revisitation, and exploration of alternatives. Adopt

translated_title: 空间中的对话：日常使用中的非线性大语言模型交互
translated_abstract: 随着大语言模型对话的不断增长，其历史记录中包含了不同的探索方向、决策以及不断演进的思路，仅通过聊天界面很难对这些内容进行浏览。我们研究了一种交互概念，通过两个同步视图来表示同一对话：一个是用户熟悉的线性聊天视图，用于持续的对话交流；另一个是空间画布视图，用于导航对话中涌现出的结构。为了研究这一交互概念，我们开发了CanvasConvo系统，它允许对话分支出替代路径，且这些路径在两个视图中均可访问。在一项有24名参与者参与的为期五天的实地部署研究中，我们考察了人们如何在自主导向的知识工作中运用这种并行表示。参与者有选择地在两个视图之间切换，而非用画布完全取代聊天。聊天仍然是对话交互的核心，而画布则支持总览、回顾以及探索替代方案。
tldr: 研究者开发了CanvasConvo系统，通过线性聊天与空间画布两个同步视图呈现LLM对话结构，为期五天的实地研究表明：聊天仍是交互核心，而画布支持对话的总览、回顾与替代路径探索。
en_tdlr: CanvasConvo represents LLM conversations through synchronized linear chat and spatial canvas views, and a five-day field deployment with 24 participants shows that chat remains central to interaction while the canvas supports overview, revisitation, and exploration of alternative conversation paths.
